title: Babette Assiette — Plates from France
metaDescription: One-of-one plates and tableware, found in France, sold from the Babette table. When they’re gone, they’re gone.
heading: BABETTE
ASSIETTE
intro: Plates we found in France and couldn’t leave behind. Brocantes, farmhouse kitchens, the odd château clearance — carried home, washed by hand, sold one by one. When a plate is gone, it’s gone.
caption: Assiette — French for plate. Prices include UK postage. Sets sold whole.
subject: Assiette — plate claimed
reserveIntro: Plates go to whoever writes first. Tell us which one, and we’ll reply within the day with payment details and a posting date.

success.message: Held. We’ll write within the day — first come, first served, and you came first.

products.name: The Limoges Eight
products.story: A full dinner service from a house outside Limoges — gilt edges softened by a century of Sunday lunches.

products.name: Café des Sports
products.story: Bistro-ware from a shuttered café in Béziers, the name still printed under the glaze.

products.name: The Barbotine Cabbage
products.story: A majolica cabbage-leaf server, absurd and magnificent. The centre of any table it lands on.

products.name: Faïence de Gien, Mismatched
products.story: Six dessert plates, no two alike, all singing the same blue. Collected one market at a time.

products.name: The Oyster Dozen
products.story: Two majolica oyster plates the colour of the Étang de Thau at low tide.

products.name: Grand Plat de Mariage
products.story: A serving platter painted for a wedding we know nothing about — initials E & C, forever.

products.name: The Absinthe Saucers
products.story: Five café saucers with the price of a pour baked into the rim. Coasters with a past.

products.name: Digoin Confiture Pots
products.story: Stoneware jam pots, still faintly sweet. Pencils, spoons, single stems — they hold anything beautifully.
